title: The Evening Brief: Hrgovic's late stoppage of Itauma tops a heavy Sunday
dek: Rosters were finalized league-wide by the 6 p.m. cutdown deadline, a Colts receiver was arrested on DWI charges hours after his preseason debut, and boxing's presumed next heavyweight star was stopped in the ninth round instead of crowned.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Sunday's biggest storylines all turned on things not going to plan: Itauma's late-fight collapse, Ohtani's stalled return, and an arrest that immediately complicates the Colts' receiver depth just as rosters were being finalized.
bottom_line: Sunday's theme was things not going as expected: a heavily favored boxer collapsed in the ninth round after leading every card, a newly signed Colts receiver was arrested hours after his preseason debut, and Ohtani's pitching return slipped again without a new target date. Roster cutdown day proceeded on schedule across the NFL, and the Rays' stadium funding cleared both required votes after years of uncertainty. The reporting establishes what happened in each case but does not explain Itauma's physical fade beyond his opponent's account, nor does it detail the cause of Ohtani's continued soreness. Coming checkpoints include the Springboks-All Blacks series decider in Johannesburg next Saturday, Hrgovic's next opponent, the Colts' handling of Allen's arrest, and whether Ohtani or Wetherholt receive updated return timelines.
body: The day's clearest thread is reversal. Moses Itauma, unbeaten in 14 fights and framed all week as a coronation waiting to happen, led Filip Hrgovic on the judges' cards through eight rounds before fading and losing by ninth-round TKO, the first time Itauma had ever fought past six rounds. Sunday also brought a stadium deal that finally closed after years of uncertainty, a marquee return to the injured-list column for the Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani, and the NFL's roster cutdown deadline colliding almost immediately with an arrest.

On the roster side, all 32 NFL teams trimmed to 53 players by the 6 p.m. ET deadline. The Bears traded 2023 second-round pick Gervon Dexter to the Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips and a fifth-round pick, and the Bills sent center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger to the Colts for a 2027 sixth-round pick, sending back a 2027 seventh-round pick. Odell Beckham Jr. made the Giants' initial 53-man roster after missing all of 2025, reuniting with head coach John Harbaugh ahead of the opener against Dallas. Hours before those roster stories broke, Colts receiver Keenan Allen, who signed with Indianapolis less than two weeks ago, was arrested in downtown Indianapolis on preliminary charges of DWI and DWI endangering a person, with blood alcohol content measured at 0.08 or more, per the Indianapolis Metro Police Department. The arrest came hours after Allen's Colts preseason debut, a 25-16 loss to Detroit in which he caught one pass for 24 yards.

In baseball, the Red Sox activated outfielder Roman Anthony and shortstop Trevor Story from the injured list ahead of Sunday's series finale against the Yankees, with Anthony batting leadoff as designated hitter after both missed more than three months. The Cardinals moved the other direction, placing Rookie of the Year candidate JJ Wetherholt on the injured list with right wrist tendinitis after weeks of playing through discomfort. Ohtani will not pitch Sunday, with Dodgers manager Dave Roberts saying he is "not 100%" and offering no revised timeline, though the team still expects him back on the mound this season. Meanwhile Pete Crow-Armstrong hit three home runs in the Cubs' 17-5 win over the Reds on August 29, intensifying his NL MVP race against Ohtani, who has won four of the past five MVP awards. MLB separately suspended a Dominican prospect from the Guardians after investigators found an elaborate age-fraud scheme, including falsified records and a staged gravesite, that led the club to cancel a 2.8 million pound agreement.

On the business and international side, Tampa City Council and the Hillsborough County Commission both approved their shares of a combined $876 million in public funding for the Rays' new $2.36 billion stadium, clearing groundbreaking targeted for later this year and an opening planned for 2029. The NFL and NFLPA remain in active negotiations over terms for player participation in 2028 Olympic flag football, with injury insurance, salary-cap credit, and scheduling still unresolved despite more than 200 players expressing interest. In rugby, South Africa beat New Zealand 33-26 in Cape Town to level their series 1-1, with Cheslin Kolbe scoring 18 points and earning player of the match; the series decider is next Saturday in Johannesburg. And in college football, Bill Belichick's UNC team beat TCU 15-10 in Ireland in the season opener, a reversal from a 48-14 loss to the same opponent last year, with UNC committing only 3 penalties for 20 yards against TCU's 11 penalties for 89 yards.

Why these things happened varies by story. The Itauma result is attributed by Hrgovic himself to recognizing early fatigue and pushing when his opening came; the reporting does not otherwise explain the physical collapse beyond noting Itauma had never fought past six rounds. Allen's arrest has no stated cause beyond the police-reported blood alcohol reading. The Rays' funding cleared after what Front Office Sports describes as politically tenuous votes, 4-3 in Tampa and 5-2 in Hillsborough County. Ohtani's delay is described only as continuing soreness, with no medical detail beyond Roberts calling him not 100 percent. The reporting does not specify further causes where those are the limits of what is known.
Desk boards were unavailable this run, so the scoreboard section is skipped; all figures above come directly from today's published stories.

The coming days carry several specific checkpoints. Itauma's recovery and next steps, and whether Hrgovic faces Frank Sanchez or a unification bout with WBC champion Agit Kabayal, are both open. The Springboks and All Blacks meet in the series decider next Saturday at altitude in Johannesburg. UNC hosts ETSU on September 12 at noon. The Rays' project moves toward a targeted groundbreaking later this year, with a 2029 opening. Ohtani's next start remains unscheduled, and the Colts face an immediate decision on Allen's roster status and any Personal Conduct Policy review. Wetherholt's IL timeline and Anthony and Story's readiness after long absences will shape both the Cardinals' and Red Sox's final stretch runs.
